summary: In Greek mythology, Eurydamas (Ancient Greek: Εὐρυδάμᾱς) was one of Penelope's suitors on Ithaca who offered her a pair of earrings with three clustering drops and was slain by Odysseus when the hall ran with blood.

sections.heading: Suitor and gift-giver
paragraphs: In Odyssey 18, when the wooers brought gifts to win Penelope, Eurydamas' squires brought him earrings with three clustering drops — bright among the gold and amber laid before the queen. In the slaughter of Book 22 Odysseus smote him among the throng as spears flew and the doors were locked.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: This atlas entry (eurydamas-ithaca) is the Ithacan suitor. Distinct from Eurydamas son of Aegyptus slain by his Danaid bride; from the Argonaut Eurydamas of Ctimene; from the Trojan dream-interpreter whose sons Abas and Polyidus Diomedes killed; and from other Trojan Eurydamases in later epic.
